data.name: Nandkishor
data.gender_notes: Nandkishor is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nand means joy, bliss, pleasure, or delight. Kishor means youth, a young man, or the giver of happiness. Together, Nandkishor means the one who bestows joy and happiness. The name Nandkishor carries the meaning “Joy (Nand) Giver of Happiness (Kishor)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nandkishor usually hope their child will grow to embody joy (nand) giver of happiness (kishor) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the attainment of inner peace and joy.
data.etymology: Nandkishor belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Joy (Nand) Giver of Happiness (Kishor).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nandkishor total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nandkishor holds profound significance in Hindu culture. Nand refers to Lord Shiva's name, symbolizing joy and happiness. Kishor is a Sanskrit word that represents the youth and vitality of Lord Krishna. The combination of these two names is often used to denote the harmony and balance between Shiva (the ultimate reality and destroyer of ego) and Krishna (the deity of love, joy, and beauty). This name invokes the essence of these two gods, embodying the true meaning of sacred union in Hinduism.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nandkishor is believed to have profound spiritual significance in Hinduism. It symbolizes the harmony between the dualistic aspects of life - the eternal truth represented by Lord Shiva and the joyful and transient aspect symbolized by Lord Krishna. This name reminds us to embrace both the reality of suffering and painful experiences (Shiva) as well as the happiness and joy found in life (Krishna). The name also signifies the desire to be a giver of joy and happiness to others, embodying the qualities of both Shiva and Krishna.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nand means "bliss" or "joy", Kishor means "youthful" or "young". Thus, Nandkishor symbolizes the joyful and youthful spirit, embodying the essence of happiness in one's youth.

historical_references.reference: Nandkishor was an important Maratha general under the rule of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He played a crucial role in the Battle of Pratapgarh in 1659, where Shivaji was crowned as the Chhatrapati of the Maratha Confederacy.
historical_references.context: Battle of Pratapgarh, Maratha Confederacy, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

historical_references.reference: Nandkishor was also a prominent poet and writer in Marathi language during the late 17th century. His works include 'Vyankalas and Vyankalas II' which are considered important contributions to Marathi literature.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Nandkishor continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
